newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore STI index up 2.2 pct as tranches narrow.
newsitem.headline: Singapore STI index up 2.2 pct as tranches narrow.

text.p: Singapore's benchmark Straits Times Industrials (STI) Index surged 2.2 percent, or 41.62 points, to 1,933.39 by 0145 GMT as the local tranches of blue chip companies continued to rise, dealers said.
Several well-known Singapore companies, including all four of the big banks, Singapore Airlines (SIA), and the monopoly publisher Singapore Press (SPH), have split listings on strategic grounds.
The local tranches of SIA and SPH are both included in the 30-share STI and were largely responsible for early surge in the index on Friday, dealers said.
The local tranches can only be bought by Singaporeans or Singapore companies. Foreign tranches can be bought by anyone.
But the government-owned Singapore Technologies group has scrapped the dual listings of five of its units in the last week, leading to speculation that other companies may follow suit.
Foreign tranches traditionally hold a premium over local tranches and tend to be much more volatile. Scrapping the split between the tranches would remove this price differential.

Elsewhere on the market, shares in hotel group Amara Holdings jumped 80 percent to a high of S$0.54 on their first day of trading. The public portion of its initial public offer (IPO) was 39.6 times subscribed at S$0.30 each.
